messages:
Maya (SRE): 09:02 — :rotating_light: Seeing a sudden spike in 403s from the public API. Error rate jumped ~15% in the last 3m. Sample: 'permission_denied: scope mismatch'. Any recent auth deploys?
Jordan (Eng): 09:03 — I rolled out a small change to the authz header mapping at 08:58 to normalize incoming SSO headers. It passed canary. Rolling back now to confirm.
Lee (Support): 09:04 — Customers starting to file in Support with 403 on embed/feature endpoints. One customer says they have valid tokens but get 403 when calling /v1/generate. Ticket IDs coming in.
Samira (Platform): 09:04 — @Jordan can you share the flag and exact config you pushed? We need to know if it affects token lookup keys.
Jordan (Eng): 09:05 — Pushing the rollback (auth-service v2.14.1 -> v2.14.0). The change was: normalize X-SSO-Role -> X-Redwood-Role mapping and changed default header precedence. Canary showed no issues but looks like role binding lookup missed for federated tokens.
Maya (SRE): 09:06 — Rolling mitigation: add temporary routing rule to send traffic to the older pool (dedicated nodes) and reduce auth service concurrency for the new instances. @@auth-bot kick off.
auth-bot: 09:06 — deploy-bot: Routing change applied to 10% of prod traffic to stable pool.
Lee (Support): 09:07 — Escalating to priority P1; customers impacted on EU and US regions. Not yet APAC. Adding affected customer list to the ticket thread.
Jordan (Eng): 09:09 — Found repro locally: when X-Redwood-Role absent and X-SSO-Role present, the new mapper set role->"" instead of preserving federated claims, causing authz service to treat the token as lacking roles. Repro steps:
```
# reproduce locally (auth dev env)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-with-federated-roles>" -H "X-SSO-Role: federated-admin" https://auth.dev.redwood/api/check
# expected: 200, roles: [federated-admin]
# observed with new mapping: 403, roles: []
```
Samira (Platform): 09:10 — That explains the permission complaints. Why did canary miss it? Canary traffic lacked federated SSO headers (we only had internal clients). Need to expand canary fixtures.
Maya (SRE): 09:12 — Rolling back the header-mapping change now. Jordan, ETA on full rollback?
Jordan (Eng): 09:13 — Rollback completed at 09:15. auth-service instances restarted to v2.14.0. Monitoring metrics: 403 rate starting to fall but some lag due to cache TTL.
Maya (SRE): 09:18 — Observing gradual recovery; 403s down to baseline after ~10m. We think there's an additional propagation/caching layer (api-proxy) that cached the denial response for short TTL (~60s) and amplified hits.
Lee (Support): 09:20 — Sending customer-facing note: "We briefly rolled back a configuration that affected SSO role mapping. Most requests recovered within 10 minutes; if you're still seeing errors, please include request-id and region." Draft pinned to the ticket.
Jordan (Eng): 09:25 — Post-rollback investigation: root cause = mapping change + insufficient canary fixture coverage + proxy cached 401/403 responses without validating auth change headers. Also a regression in the authz library: when header mapping produces empty role header, the library treats it as explicit deny instead of missing -> fallback.
Samira (Platform): 09:27 — Action items: expand canary fixtures to include federated tokens; add unit test for empty->preserve semantics; patch proxy to avoid caching auth failures for 120s, and add a short-circuit to bypass cache on header changes.
Maya (SRE): 09:29 — Mitigations completed: rollback ✅, routing fallback ✅, proxy cache TTL increased for error responses to 5s (temporary), alerting rule updated to trigger on auth header mismatch rate.
Lee (Support): 09:34 — Support checklist for customers still affected: collect `x-request-id`, `region`, `Authorization` token (redact token to last 4 chars), `X-SSO-Role` header value, and time window. Use this curl to repro (redact token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-SSO-Role: <value>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Jordan (Eng): 09:40 — Patch PR opened to restore preserve semantics in the mapper + add unit tests: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/auth/pull/642 (WIP). Also adding a canary job that replays federated-token traces.
Samira (Platform): 09:45 — We'll schedule a follow-up postmortem at 14:00 today. Please add timeline notes and links to customer tickets.
Maya (SRE): 09:46 — Current status: service degraded -> recovering. If the 403 rate creeps back up, we'll re-open and consider a temporary global throttle to reduce bad cache amplification.
Lee (Support): 09:49 — Updating customers with ETA and workaround. :thumbsup:
auth-bot: 09:50 — incident-tracker: Incident created INC-2026-032, severity P1 -> In progress.
Jordan (Eng): 10:02 — Quick log snippet for postmortem: "mapper: incoming header X-SSO-Role='federated-admin' -> mapped X-Redwood-Role='' (bug) -> authz denied".
Maya (SRE): 10:05 — Leaving notes here for postmortem: repro steps, timeline, affected regions, support tickets, and the short-term mitigations. Will attach graphs to the PM doc.
Samira (Platform): 10:10 — Thanks everyone. Follow-up: add end-to-end canary that includes real federated SSO headers and verify proxy caching behavior before future auth rollouts.
Lee (Support): 10:20 — Closing thread for now; will reopen if new customer reports come in.
